summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for ileal conduit urinary diversion due to severe urinary incontinence causing recurrent skin breakdown and stage IV pressure ulcers. The surgery was performed successfully, and he recovered without intraoperative complications. Post-operatively, he developed a fever on POD4, prompting a CT scan that showed nonspecific post-surgical changes without abscess or pneumonia. Urine culture grew E. coli, leading to a seven-day course of meropenem. His white count improved, and he transitioned from IV to oral pain medication. The NG tube was removed on POD2, diet advanced, and ostomy care was taught. On POD11, ureteral stents and the PICC line were removed, staples were replaced with Steri-Strips, and he was discharged home with visiting nurse services. He refused Bactrim initiation in the hospital but agreed to take it at home. Follow-up was arranged with urology, plastics, and primary care.
